description: Controlled subjects with declared defects, plus this repository's own artwork. Covers every failure mode T-012, T-018 and T-013 found, aimed rather than exhaustive: negative controls, the 1px-margin trap, the 4-vs-8 connectivity decision, the compactnessQ gate, the multi-frame rules, and §4.2 in two parts — the form-conformance term as a straight band against a form-following contour, a level set against both and a straight terminator on a straight-edged form, then one case per single-code defect in §4.2's issue table, so that a hue-carried form, a crushed shadow and a blown highlight are each something a case says they mean. Every expectation here is derived by hand from docs/EVALUATION.md and the declared geometry of the case, never copied out of the pipeline's own output.

cases.label: A 10x8 block with a 3px margin all round: one mass, nothing touching an edge

defects.note: Nothing injected. The baseline negative control: an analyzer that fires here is worse than one that misses a defect.

cases.label: A standing figure whose legs are joined to the body and split from each other: the gap is a background channel, not a hole

defects.note: Nothing injected. The second negative control, and the one that pins the holes/background pairing from the other side: a deliberate gap between two legs is exactly the shape a 4-connected background would call a hole.

cases.label: A 32x32 figure built from six overlapping rectangles: head, torso, two arms, two legs

defects.note: Nothing injected. Six rects rather than one, because a union of rectangles is where a naive component count goes wrong: five of the six touch the others only along an edge, and the pair of legs does not touch at all without the torso joining them.

cases.label: A 48x16 banner on a non-square 64x24 canvas: the UI slice, and a canvas that is not square

defects.note: Nothing injected. Present because docs/EVALUATION.md 6.3 asks for non-square canvases and because a threshold that only works at 32x32 is not a threshold.

cases.label: A solid body with a 0.39-alpha glow beside it: partial alpha is counted and never scored

defects.note: Nothing injected. Pins the ALPHA_SOLID decision from context.ts: a glow at 0 < alpha < 128 is a design decision, not a body part, so it must not enter N, must not change components, and must not become part of a contour. The glow is placed clear of the body on purpose: the first version of this case overlapped it, and the composited overlap stopped being partial alpha, which is a second and much less obvious way for a fixture to teach the wrong thing.

cases.label: A 16x16 disc on 32x32 with the outline command grown one pixel outside it

defects.note: Nothing injected. Exists for its connectivity count, and it refines docs/EVALUATION.md 3.3's prose: a CLOSED contour is 4-connected, because every turn is joined by the corner pixel. The claim that a 1px contour is '8-connected and 4-disconnected' holds for a staircase RUN, which is what connectivity/contour-staircase-24 isolates, and not for a closed ring.

cases.label: A 12px 1px diagonal run from (2,2) to (13,13): one component under 8-connectivity, twelve under 4

defects.note: 12 components under the subject rule, so the analyzer is right to say so: a shape whose parts touch only at a corner falls in half at 0.5x scale.
compactnessQ 65. A 1px diagonal is the thinnest thing a sprite can be.
Largest piece is 1 of 12 px.

cases.label: Two 5x5 blocks meeting at a single corner: one mass under 8-connectivity, two under 4

defects.note: One stray of 25 px against a 50 px subject, so the -75 row fires. share is exactly 500/1000, which is why fragmented-silhouette must NOT fire: the comparison is strict.

cases.label: A 5x5 block with one pixel punched out and a corner erased, so the pocket reaches the outside through a diagonal only

defects.note: Nothing injected, and that is the finding: the 1px pocket at (3,3) IS a hole under 4-connectivity and is NOT a hole here, because the erased corner at (2,2) is 4-connected to the outside and 8-connected to the pocket. The test proves the discriminating half by running the same flood with a 4-connected background and getting 1.

cases.label: An 18px 1px diagonal run on 24x24: the configuration docs/EVALUATION.md 3.3 describes for a contour

defects.note: 18 components under 4-connectivity.
compactnessQ 44.
Largest piece is 1 of 18 px.

cases.label: A 12x12 body with a 3x3 speck floating four pixels away from it

defects.note: One stray of 9 px against a 153 px subject: past the 2/100 stray ratio, so the -75 row.

cases.label: A body with a hat floating three rows above it: one dominant mass, so not fragmented

defects.note: One stray of 24 px against a 120 px subject. share is 800/1000, comfortably clear of the fragmented-silhouette floor, so this is the counter-case to defect/three-masses-20: two components, and only one of the two codes fires.

cases.label: Three blocks of 25, 20 and 15 px: no dominant mass, and the score floors at 0

defects.note: Two strays, so the -150 row rather than -75.
Largest is 25 of 60 px, share 417/1000. Blocking at severity 0.70.

cases.label: A 20x20 body with one pixel punched out: the area <= 3 clause of interior-hole

defects.note: A 1 px hole, which fires the 'any hole with area <= 3' clause rather than the ratio clause. Half of defect/interior-hole-window-24's contrast pair.

cases.label: The same body with a 6x6 window cut out: the holeRatio clause of interior-hole

defects.note: A 36 px hole, which is past the 'area <= 3' clause and so fires only because holeRatio is 99/1000. The other half of the contrast pair: same body, same code, same -100, from a different clause.

cases.label: A 12x12 ring with an 8x8 hole: the documented false positive, a deliberately hollow asset

defects.note: A 64 px hole in an 80 px ring. docs/EVALUATION.md 4.1 names this as a known false positive that a human rater's note settles, and no measurement can tell a keyhole from a mistake. In the corpus it is a defect like any other, because the mechanical rule is the mechanical rule.
compactnessQ 157: a 1px wall really is thin, whatever the wall is for.

cases.label: Ink running to three canvas edges with a 2px guard on the fourth: measured, and blocking

defects.note: borderTouch 3, severity 0.80, blocking. This is the exact boundary of SUBJECT_REQUIRED_MARGIN: 2px of guard is a margin somebody chose, so the dimension applies, and a shape cropped on three sides IS clipped. The two neighbours in the margin-guard pair show what happens at 0px and 1px.

cases.label: A 12x12 subject inside a 64x64 canvas: under a quarter of an edge on both axes

defects.note: span 188/1000. The comparison is an OR of two strict `<` tests, so a subject under a quarter on EITHER axis is undersized.

cases.label: A 16x16 canvas with nothing on it: every dimension reports 1000 and one blocking issue fails it

defects.note: docs/EVALUATION.md 5.3's demonstration. A blank canvas is not bad artwork, it is NO artwork, and a mean cannot express that: the score is 1.00 and the verdict is fail. This case exists so that a change which turns the blank canvas into a low score, or into an exclusion, fails.

cases.label: A 32x32 canvas inked edge to edge: no subject, so no silhouette is reported at all

defects.note: Nothing was injected; this is the ten real full-bleed scenes in miniature, and it is where T-012's bug lived. Measured on its own the mask scores 800 with a blocking shape-clipped, because borderTouch is 4 whenever ink runs to the frame. The report does not say that: it says the dimension does not apply, and records why.

cases.label: The same ink with a single transparent row at the bottom: still no subject, and the raw measurement is still 800

defects.note: Nothing injected. The knife-edge T-018 found and solved: identical ink, one pixel of frame, and the predicate has to answer 'cannot measure' rather than 'a perfect subject'. The measure block below is the measurement that was never delivered, which is why the corpus records measurements even for excluded cases.

cases.label: The same ink inset by 2px on all four sides: a subject, measured, and clean

defects.note: Nothing injected. The other end of the margin-guard pair: 2px is a margin somebody chose, so the dimension applies, and what it then has to say is 'clean', not 'perfect'. Without this case the pair would only show the exclusion and a reader could not tell whether the predicate also mis-handles a real subject.

cases.label: Two frames: a clean 8x8 block, then three separate masses. The dimension carries the worst frame

defects.note: Frame 1 only: two strays, so -150.
Frame 1 only: largest is 25 of 54 px. Blocking.

cases.label: Three byte-identical frames: motion cannot be measured, and the hold is not a gate failure

defects.note: Severity 0.35, non-blocking, alongside excluded.motion = 'no-motion-content'. Not redundant: the exclusion says the dimension cannot be measured here, and the advisory says four copies of frame 0 is usually an agent that meant to animate and did not. Measured honestly, an identical sequence is a PERFECT animation, which is why the decision is the aggregator's and is made before the analyzer runs.

cases.label: Two frames, the second blank: the sheet exports as a hole and one blocking issue says so

defects.note: Severity 1.00, blocking. Note what does NOT happen: silhouette is still applicable (frame 0 has a subject, and exclusion is unanimity over inked frames, never a majority), and the blank frame is not scored rather than being scored 0, because 0 would mean 'measured, and it is bad'.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x28 rect, compactnessQ 784

defects.note: Sweep member. The roundest the sweep gets; the 30x2 member is the same rectangle twenty-six pixels shorter and nothing else changed.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 28x28 rect, compactnessQ 785

defects.note: Sweep member. The most compact a rectangle can be: 4*pi*N/P^2 for a square is pi/4, so 785 is the ceiling of this whole family.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x20 rect, compactnessQ 754

defects.note: Sweep member.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x15 rect, compactnessQ 698

defects.note: Sweep member.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x10 rect, compactnessQ 589

defects.note: Sweep member. 3:1, which is about as slender as a character silhouette gets before it stops reading.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x8 rect, compactnessQ 522

defects.note: Sweep member.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x6 rect, compactnessQ 436

defects.note: Sweep member.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x5 rect, compactnessQ 385

defects.note: Sweep member. The last member comfortably above the gate.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x4 rect, compactnessQ 326: the last member above the gate

defects.note: Sweep member, and the important one: 326 is 26 per-mille above the gate. A gate moved from 300 to 250 would have left this case passing; a gate moved to 330 would have failed it. The sweep exists so that a move can be argued about with the whole curve in front of the reader rather than with one asset.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 28x3 rect, compactnessQ 275: 25 below the gate, and 6 above the one real character sprite

defects.note: compactnessQ 275 is below the gate of 300, so thin-profile fires. This is the sweep's upper neighbour of artwork/verify/lantern-keeper.pixel at 269, and the pair of them is the closest thing this corpus has to saying 'the gate sits between these two'.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x3 rect, compactnessQ 260: 9 below the one real character sprite

defects.note: compactnessQ 260, the sweep's lower neighbour of the lantern keeper at 269. Together with sweep/rect-28x3 at 275 this brackets the real measurement with a 15-wide interval.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 34x3 rect, compactnessQ 234

defects.note: compactnessQ 234. A 1px blade at game scale; a shape this thin genuinely does not read, which is the case the gate is for.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x2 rect, compactnessQ 184: the slenderest member, and thickness-sweep's other half

defects.note: compactnessQ 184. The matched pair with sweep/rect-30x28 at 784: same width, same canvas, same 2px margin, and the ONLY difference is the height. compactnessQ separates them by 600 per-mille and scoreQ by 100, and the second number is the one to review: the whole -100 of thin-profile is doing that work, so the dimension distinguishes a blade from a slab by exactly one penalty step.

cases.label: The same 28x3 band, centred on a 32x32 canvas: a knife

defects.note: A 3px band, which is 94/1000 of the canvas's short side. Also subject-undersized, because 3*4 < 32: the two codes overlap exactly on a band, which is the honest reason both are printed on every row.
28 wide on a 32 canvas, so the subject spans under a quarter of the width — §3.7's `span < 0.25` in per-mille (94).

cases.label: The same 28x3 band, centred on a 1024x1024 canvas: a horizon

defects.note: The identical 84 pixels on a 1024x1024 canvas, so `compactnessQ` is 275 on both members — the shape descriptor is right not to move, it is the same drawing — while `thicknessQ` reads 3 against 94.
3*4 < 1024 by a wide margin, and the subject spans 498/1000 of the canvas at its widest, which is under §3.7's quarter.

cases.label: The 28x3 band magnified 32x, centred on a 1024x1024 canvas

defects.note: NEGATIVE contrast pair with `sweep/band-28x3-on-32`, and the pair is designed to come out at **zero**. This is the knife magnified 32x, and every ratio of two lengths in one sprite is invariant under uniform magnification, so every measurement is identical and every one of them should be: compactnessQ 275, thicknessQ 94, profileQ 94, scoreQ 700. The one column where they are 32x apart is `thicknessPx`, a pixel count rather than a ratio — 96 against 3. Separating them further would need a target resolution, which a `.pixel` document does not carry and this pipeline must not invent, so the limit is pinned as an expectation rather than left in a comment. A corpus that only carried the pairs it passes would be hiding this one.

96*4 < 1024, and the subject spans 875/1000 of the canvas at its widest, which is over §3.7's quarter — so this member is NOT subject-undersized on the span clause. It is declared anyway because 96*4 = 384 is not >= 1024... which is the same arithmetic; the code comes from the same gate on the short side, and both are printed on the row so a reader can see which clause fired.

cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions on docs/EVALUATION.md's 1-5 scale and give one overall judgement of usable / needs-work / unusable. This is an item icon, not a character, and §4's anchors are written for shapes, so say what you had to reinterpret.

cases.label: A 32x32 hard-surface tile: a bevelled block, the value dimension's curvature-gate counter-case
cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions and give one overall judgement. A tile is the case docs/EVALUATION.md 4.2 says it cannot judge well: its straight edges are not a sphere, so a curvature gate has to exempt it. If your silhouette score disagrees with your value score, say so in a note — that disagreement is the finding.

cases.label: A 64x64 full-bleed field with a horizon: a scene the analyzer declares UNMEASURABLE, rated by a human anyway
cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions and give one overall judgement. Note that `evaluate` reports silhouette as excluded ('no-subject') for this image and delivers no silhouette number at all, because the ink reaches the frame. Score silhouette anyway, from the picture. If a human score exists for something the pipeline says it cannot measure, T-022 needs to know which side is wrong.

cases.label: Five straight 45-degree tone bands cut corner to corner across the same 25-row round body `pixel demo` draws, on 32x32

defects.note: The same five tones, the same contrast and the same body as `value/nested-contour-32`, banded on `x + y` instead of laid on as translations of the row table. Every boundary is a straight line across a round form, so the shape reads and the tone count is right, and the only thing wrong with it is that the boundaries do not follow the form. This is the half of §4.2's acceptance pair that should fail.

cases.label: The same body shaded with four nested translated contours — `pixel demo`'s own construction

defects.note: The correction to `value/straight-diagonal-32`, and the negative control for the form term. Nothing is injected: the same five tones on the same body, laid on as translations of the row table rather than as straight cuts — which is what `packages/cli/src/demo.ts` does, so the pair is drawn on the form the product actually ships. `absent` names `plane-crosses-form` because that is the one code the pair turns on.

cases.label: The same body shaded with true insets — four level sets of `dist`, 2px apart, the construction that looks like a target

defects.note: The level-set bias, as a control rather than as a claim. §4.2 measures the spread of `dist` along a plane boundary, and a level set has a spread near zero, so the specified term rated this the best possible construction and rated `value/nested-contour-32` the worst — even though the two are the same body with the same five tones, the same five planes and the same four boundaries. The report prints both: `spanQ unscored` reads 91 here against 909 there, and `crossesQ` is 0 on all four of these boundaries because a level set turns everywhere, which is the property the scored term was redesigned around. The 909 was 545 until `dirQ` was made invariant to whether a boundary closes, at which point all four boundaries here and all four in `value/nested-contour-32` read `crossesQ` 0, and the worst plane stopped being a worst plane at all. Two things about the drawing, both load-bearing. The insets are 2px apart, not 1px: a 1px level set is a line, no pixel of it has three same-tone orthogonal neighbours, and it is therefore not a plane at all — a 1px version of this case registered 34 tone regions and ZERO plane boundaries, because a 1px staircase contour is 8-connected and 4-disconnected, so its 33 fragments each read as a region of their own. And the four insets are drawn largest-first, because a deeper inset painted before a shallower one is overpainted by it: the other order leaves two tones on the canvas instead of five.

cases.label: A straight-edged box with a straight horizontal terminator: correct shading, and the curvature gate must spare it

defects.note: §4.2 says "a straight plane across a straight-edged form is correct, not wrong", and the curvature gate is the clause that delivers it. This is the gate's negative control and it is the only case that can catch a gate which has been made so permissive that it never fires anywhere.

cases.label: One lightness bucket in four hues: the form is carried by hue, which a game tint takes away

defects.note: Every interior boundary changes hue without changing `LqBucket`, so hue is doing the work tone should.
One bucket holds 1000/1000 of the solid pixels.
The four hues sit at Lq 117..119, so the range is 2 against a floor of 45.

cases.label: The lower 16 rows of the same body at Lq 9: the shadow side has run out of steps

defects.note: 16 of the body's 25 rows are at or below Lq 12, which is past the 30/100 share.

cases.label: The same form-following construction with its lightest plane run to white: the lit side has run out of headroom

defects.note: One plane of the same five, repainted at Lq 255 instead of 220. 159 of the body's 398 solid pixels are at or above Lq 243, which is 399/1000 against §4.2's 10/100 share. The only difference from `value/nested-contour-32` is that one swatch, which is what makes the two a §6.2 pair: the tone terms separate them and every shape reading is identical.
